analyst_view.overall: Inter (15th, 6 points) and Stuttgart (14th, 7 points) both want to climb towards the top eight, and Inter still face Dortmund and Liverpool later. Inter get Lautaro Martínez back: Italian press expected only a few minutes for him at Atalanta on Sunday so he can start against Stuttgart, and Hakan Çalhanoglu is available (no ban reported, and the numbers no longer assume one); Ange-Yoan Bonny (counted) and Zielinski are out. Stuttgart drew 0-0 at Schalke on Saturday; Angelo Stiller (counted out) has missed games since late October with an adductor problem, but Sebastian Hoeneß says a comeback at Inter is possible and will be decided late, and Vagnoman (counted) is out. No referee is named yet. My only move is a small lift on goals for Lautaro starting, which the numbers' recent form did not include.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals and already take Bonny off Inter (-4.7%) and Stiller and Vagnoman off Stuttgart (about -14%). Lautaro, Inter's captain and main scorer, is set to start after a month out, which their recent form (-1.3%) did not have, and Stiller may yet return for Stuttgart, so I lean a little higher, to about 3.4. Stiller is only a possibility, which keeps the lean small.

corners.text: The numbers expect 10 corners, 6.1 of them Inter's, already up about 5% for Inter's recent corner count. Inter's wing-backs Dimarco and Spence are fit and Stuttgart press high, which fits the usual picture, so I stay at 10.

cards.text: The numbers expect 3.8 cards and already take a little off both sides for their recent cards. The referee is not named yet; Stuttgart's pressing produces some fouls, and there is no rivalry. I found nothing new, so I stay at about 3.8.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.8 shots and already add about 16% to Inter's side for their recent shooting and take 6% off Stuttgart's. Inter at home needing a win should shoot plenty, but that is already in the numbers, so I stay at about 32.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target, up a little for Inter and down 6% for Stuttgart's recent accuracy. Lautaro back sharpens Inter, but Thuram and Esposito have been carrying the line well enough, and the goals lift covers his effect. I stay at about 10.
